text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Saddam Hussein chairs cabinet meeting and says Iraq's socialist system is different from that pursued by communist parties.
- Saddam says Iraq's economy is in good shape and has adapted to pressures from U.N. trade sanctions.
- Saddam says Iraq's factories are in fine shape and urges the socialist sector to employ private principles in its work.
- Iraq urges U.N. to force Turkey to withdraw its troops from northern Iraq.
- Syrian trade delegation arrives in Baghdad.
- Jordan wants a halt to the inspection of goods destined for Iraq under the oil-for-food deal.
(The above were also carried by AL-IRAQ and JUMHOURIYA)
- Article on the significance of the forthcoming census to be undertaken late this year.
- Article on the relations of Arab countries with their non- Arab neighbours.
- Jordanian and Iraqi chambers of commerce sign cooperation deal.
- Qatar's foreign minister says Gulf Arab countries are keen to preserve Iraq's territorial integrity.
- Trade minister meets Spanish trade official.
